# Welcome {.unnumbered}

The **ivDiag** package provides tools for estimation, inference, sensitivity analysis, and visualization with instrumental variable (IV) designs. It implements the guidelines proposed in @lal2023trust in **R**, enabling researchers to obtain reliable and robust estimates of their IV models.

The package computes several types of standard errors (SEs), *F*-statistics, and weak-IV robust confidence intervals (CIs). Together they show how uncertain an IV estimate is, including when the instruments are weak.

The package also provides the Anderson-Rubin (AR) test and adjusted *t*-ratio inference from @lee2022valid to enhance the validity and reliability of statistical inference.

**ivDiag** also offers the Local-to-Zero (LTZ) estimator [@conley2012plausibly]. This estimator adjusts the 2SLS estimate and its confidence interval for a plausible violation of the exclusion restriction specified by the researcher. Functions for plotting coefficients from two-stage least squares (2SLS) and ordinary least squares (OLS) regressions allow researchers to compare the two estimators and various inferential methods.

The omnibus function `ivDiag` returns a list. Parts of this list can be appended as additional rows in tables produced by `modelsummary`, `fixest::etable`, and stargazer, among other tools. This makes it easy for researchers to integrate `ivDiag` estimates into their existing workflows.

**ivDiag** applies only to the **one-treatment** case, although there can be multiple instruments.

## Organization

-   [Chapter @sec-start]\
    Installation and the datasets shipped with the package.

-   [Chapter @sec-estimation]\
    The omnibus function `ivDiag()` and the coefficient plot, using @mcclendon2014.

-   [Chapter @sec-tests]\
    The effective *F* statistic, the AR test, and the *tF* procedure run separately, including an AR set under a weak instrument.

-   [Chapter @sec-rd]\
    Fuzzy regression discontinuity designs.

-   [Chapter @sec-sensitivity]\
    Zero-first-stage tests and the local-to-zero adjustment, using @guiso2016long.
